note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor (authored none of the userns spec commits d8427e4380, b00e3c6710, 68b723ec4f, 7d11a51269). userns.Enter (internal/test/userns/userns_linux.go) re-executes the one test in a new user+net+mount namespace and returns false in the parent only after the child's own PASS line; a child failure, a zero-exit failure or a child that selected nothing fails the parent, and a child skip skips it, so the guard cannot turn a red into a green. Section 8.1: "On these interfaces, the IP source should be set to any of the other IP addresses belonging to the router.  For this reason, there must be at least one IP address assigned to the router." Unit changes read: the guard; CAP_NET_RAW probe fails instead of skipping; and the positive now adds a link-scope route to the peer's 10.255.0.2/32 over the unnumbered device, because the child namespace has no host default route and loose rp_filter needs a route back to the reply's source. That route is what OSPF would install on a real unnumbered link; it has no preferred source, so it cannot supply the donor address, and it does not bear on the outgoing multicast's source, which the test still compares exactly: getsockopt IP_MULTICAST_IF == donor, and the peer reads the IP header source == 10.255.0.1 with the exact payload. The reply to AllSPFRouters must still arrive on the unnumbered device's socket, so the membership-on-the-borrower assertion is intact. The removed comment about Alpine's strict rp_filter described the old host and is correctly replaced. Negative TestOSPFRefusesDeviceWithoutRouterAddress: guard only; with no IPv4 address in the namespace and a kernel control proving the join works without one, the backend must refuse and name the missing address. Mutant records (multicastDevice ifindex->0; interfaceIPv4 error->nil) were re-recorded in d8427e4380 and are current per the gate. The setReversePath comment change is accurate to the new lab.
